To correct the PDDL plan based on the provided object list and instructions, we need to ensure that the variable names directly reflect the objects and their locations. Here's the corrected plan:

```lisp
; Define the durative actions for the tasks

; Durative action for preparing hot water for a shower
(:durative-action PrepareHotWaterForShower
  :parameters (?robot - Robot ?faucet - Faucet)
  :duration (= ?duration 5) ; Assume it takes 5 time units
  :condition (and
    (at start (not (inaction ?robot)))
    (at start (at ?robot ?faucet))
  )
  :effect (and
    (at start (switch-on ?robot ?faucet))
    (at end (switch-off ?robot ?faucet))
  )
)

; Durative action for putting toilet paper in the trash
(:durative-action PutToiletPaperInTrash
  :parameters (?robot - Robot ?toiletPaper - ToiletPaper ?garbageCan - GarbageCan)
  :duration (= ?duration 3) ; Assume it takes 3 time units
  :condition (and
    (at start (not (inaction ?robot)))
    (at start (at ?robot ?toiletPaper))
    (at start (holding ?robot ?toiletPaper))
    (at start (at ?robot ?garbageCan))
  )
  :effect (and
    (at end (at-location ?toiletPaper ?garbageCan))
    (at end (not (holding ?robot ?toiletPaper)))
  )
)

; Plan execution using timed durative actions
; Assume the initial state has robots at their respective starting locations

; Robot 2 prepares hot water for shower
(0.0: (PrepareHotWaterForShower robot2 Faucet))

; Robot 3 puts toilet paper in the trash
(0.0: (PutToiletPaperInTrash robot3 ToiletPaper GarbageCan))
```
